description: Giuseppe Verdi turns Italian opera into a political weapon and a theater of the soul: Rigoletto, La Traviata, Aida, Otello.

hero.hook: From a chorus of slaves to tricolor flags: when opera united Italy.

blocks.text: **Giuseppe Verdi** (**1813**-**1901**) was more than the greatest Italian opera composer of the 19th century. He was the musical voice of Italian unity, and the man who pushed the form toward a new psychological realism.

From *Rigoletto* to *La Traviata*, his works left the drawing room to talk about politics, honor, love and injustice. Against the German **Richard Wagner**, Verdi stayed faithful to Italian melodic clarity, but made the drama far denser.

**Opera**, born in Florence around **1600**, was the great European entertainment of the 19th century. Early in the century [[Bel canto]] ruled: vocal virtuosity and beautiful melodies. **Rossini** and **Donizetti** dominated.

Verdi admired these masters, but found their librettos too artificial. For him, music had to serve the drama, and every note had to carry an urgency or a feeling. He adapted **Shakespeare** and **Victor Hugo**, and he thickened the orchestra. While Wagner dreamed of a total mythological artwork, Verdi anchored opera in the social reality of his own time.
In 1832, the Milan Conservatory turned Verdi down. The examiners called his hand position at the piano “defective” and his talent insufficient.

sections.title: Before Verdi: bel canto and the revolution of drama

blocks.text: In **1842**, *Nabucco* was a triumph. The opera tells of the exile of the Hebrews in Babylon. In an Italy occupied by the Austrian Empire, the slaves' chorus *Va, pensiero* became an underground anthem. Verdi became a figure of [[The Italian Risorgimento]], the movement for national unification.

blocks.caption: Va, pensiero: an opera chorus that became a patriotic anthem

blocks.text: In the 1850s, people wrote “Viva VERDI” on the walls. Behind the name hid an acronym: **Vittorio Emanuele Re D'Italia**. Verdi supported the cause and was elected to parliament in **1861** under the wing of [[Cavour]], the architect of unity. His operas put outsiders on stage against the established order: the jester of *Rigoletto*, the struggles of *Il Trovatore*.
In Venice, patriotic audiences threw green, white and red bouquets onto the stage to make up the banned Italian flag.

The “popular trilogy” set a new standard: *Rigoletto* (**1851**), *Il Trovatore* and *La Traviata* (**1853**). Ancient kings were no longer the only subject. Rigoletto is a hunchbacked jester, nothing like the noble heroes that [[Opera seria vs. opera buffa]] had made standard.

*La Traviata*, based on *The Lady of the Camellias* by **Alexandre Dumas fils**, caused a scandal: a Parisian courtesan of the day dies of tuberculosis. The censors wanted the action pushed back into the past. Verdi held firm. In **1871**, *Aida*, commissioned for Cairo and the Suez Canal, mixed spectacle with the clash between love and duty.

blocks.caption: La Traviata: the scandal of an opera too modern for its time

blocks.text: For *Aida*, Verdi had straight “Theban trumpets” built, copied from ancient Egyptian reliefs.

sections.title: Rigoletto, La Traviata, Aida: realism on stage

blocks.text: Past the age of 70, pushed by his publisher Ricordi and the librettist **Arrigo Boito**, Verdi came back with *Otello* (**1887**) and *Falstaff* (**1893**). He dropped the classical alternation between [[Recitative]] and arias for a smooth dramatic flow. *Falstaff*, written at 79, ends on a verdict: “All the world's a joke.”

When he died in **1901**, more than **300,000** people followed the funeral procession in Milan and sang *Nabucco*. He left his fortune to a retirement home for musicians. His influence fed Italian [[Verismo]] and all of modern music theater.
